attachments.title: Source clinical note
attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-09-15
Provider: Dr. Marcus Chen, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Severe epigastric abdominal pain and vomiting

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns with severe epigastric pain and vomiting with hemolytic anemia, seen in January 2020. These episodes have occurred multiple times over the past three years. His mother reports similar episodes requiring medical attention since he was a toddler.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Beta-thalassemia (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Transfusion-dependent hemolytic anemia
- Severe familial hypertriglyceridemia
- Secondary hemochromatosis
- Hepatosplenomegaly
- Recurrent acute pancreatitis

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Central venous port-a-cath placement for monthly transfusions

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Deferasirox 500 mg PO daily (iron chelation)
- Folic acid 1 mg PO daily
- Gemfibrozil 300 mg PO twice daily
- Vitamin D3 2000 IU PO daily
- Calcium carbonate 500 mg PO daily

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
Family history is negative for early cardiovascular disease, but his older sister had similar skin lesions.

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Kindergarten student.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, you note clusters of small yellow papules on his elbows, knees, and buttocks, along with a palpable liver edge and spleen tip.

LABORATORY DATA:
His fasting blood sample is described as milky and opalescent.
Laboratory evaluation reveals high chylomicrons and triglycerides. After intravenous administration of heparin, which releases endothelial-bound lipoprotein lipase into the plasma, his plasma demonstrates normal enzymatic hydrolysis of triglycerides. Genetic testing is pending.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Elena Papadopoulos, MD
Department: Pediatric Hematology and Oncology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Increasing facial changes and abdominal fullness with pallor and decreased energy

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
His parents note prominent cheekbones, frontal bossing, and bowing of his legs that have become more apparent over the past year. He has had decreased energy and appears pale but has no fever, cough, or bleeding.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Transfusion-dependent hemolytic anemia
- Severe familial hypertriglyceridemia
- Secondary hemochromatosis
- Hepatosplenomegaly
- Recurrent acute pancreatitis

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Central venous port-a-cath placement for monthly transfusions

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Deferasirox 500 mg PO daily (iron chelation)
- Folic acid 1 mg PO daily
- Gemfibrozil 300 mg PO twice daily
- Vitamin D3 2000 IU PO daily
- Calcium carbonate 500 mg PO daily

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father: Beta-thalassemia trait (carrier), hypertriglyceridemia
- Mother: Beta-thalassemia trait (carrier), hypertriglyceridemia
- Older sister: Beta-thalassemia major (alive, undergoing treatment)
- Paternal uncle: Died in childhood from complications of thalassemia

SOCIAL HISTORY:
His vaccinations are up to date and he has no recent travel history.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Physical exam shows frontal bossing, maxillary prominence, bowed legs, and hepatosplenomegaly. Neurologic exam is normal. Growth parameters are below the 10th percentile for age.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory results:
Hemoglobin                             7.2 g/dL
MCV                                      68 fL
RDW                                      14%
Serum ferritin                       80 ng/mL
Serum iron                           110 µg/dL
Serum calcium                     9.2 mg/dL
Serum vitamin D                   32 ng/mL

IMAGING:
A skull radiograph is obtained and shown below.
